items.title: Pete Barbutti interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 8, 2022
items.q: Jimmy — Robert used to wash the car for Jimmy every day.

ctx.x: Yeah we had — first of all we had to play “Dixie” to open every show, and then there were no black people allowed in there. There were no black people who were allowed in the same stores we went in, nobody at the lunch counters, nobody in the restaurants. They had their own little thing. And when we’d play certain kind of music they’d come by and they’d say, “Stop playing that — you know the N word — music.” And we had one incident where there was a young black kid worked in the restaurant, he swept up and…

to wash the car for Jimmy every day. And there was a sort of a symbolic thing with him that someday he might own a car like that. He’d wash it, he’d sit in it and you know. He was an adult. I mean he was young but he was an adult. And so on our day off Jimmy threw Robert the keys and said, “Robert, take your girlfriend for a ride just don’t drink when you’re driving.” You know, “Take your girlfriend.” Because we were going to hang out with some girl singers that were new down there, we had an apartment back…
